rv.q: All in all, the musical “Helen and Hermia” deserves to become a staple of summer outdoor theater.
This is the best show I've seen yet by the Impostors, one of the most consistently engaging and enjoyable young companies in town.
A laugh-out-loud musical, not without moments of romantic insight, might make for an exciting and playful night out this spring.
I was glad to be a part of their latest work and look forward to seeing what they try next.

Quite literally—it’s a musical based on William Shakespeare ’s play “ A Midsummer Night’s Dream ,” so the forest greenery had a ways to go. But even if the physical production wasn’t yet fully formed—and what there was was verdant, indeed—what emerged was a charming ode to love, friendship, and the unamplified voice.

cn.t: Critics praise this charming musical adaptation of "A Midsummer Night's Dream" for its strong performances, clever Shakespearean humor, and inventive staging, though at nearly three hours it significantly outlasts the original play.
